A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReSplat research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original view-synthesis experiments, generalization tests, architectural ablations, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional model-scale, initialization, and neighbor-search comparisons.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an optional local kNN procedure that searches spatial and camera-projected candidate windows instead of all points. It also specifies k=8 for recurrent attention, whereas v2 specified k=16. These are targeted changes; the compact initialization, rendering-error feedback, recurrent updates, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same DL3DV, RealEstate10K, and ACID coverage, including the existing view-count, resolution, and cross-dataset scenarios. The added experiments vary model capacity, initialization, or implementation rather than introducing new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds WorldMirror and a larger single-step ReSplat initialization as comparators. SplatFormer and depth-regularized 3DGS were already evaluated in v2 Tables 10–11. The separate qualitative Gaussian-reconstruction comparisons against DepthSplat in v2 Figures 12–13 are removed.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 559M-parameter ViT-L initialization, comparisons across MVSplat/Small/Base initializations, and global-versus-local kNN testing at eight views and 512×960 resolution. The reported recurrent neighborhood changes from 16 to 8. Existing benchmark settings and Appendix B training schedules are retained; these disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends diagnostic analysis to whether larger single-step models substitute for recurrence, how refinement depends on initialization, and the efficiency-quality tradeoff of local neighbor search (Table 2, Figure 6, Table S7). Existing architectural and generalization analyses largely remain. The two Gaussian-geometry case studies in v2 Figures 12–13 are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both present point-valued performance and runtime measurements.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive results for model scaling, initialization dependence, and local kNN. Table 2 compares recurrent Small at 29.07 dB with Large initialization at 27.86 and WorldMirror at 23.54. Table S7 reports local/global kNN at 27.65/27.70 dB and 0.591/0.816 seconds. Retained benchmark quality scores are unchanged, but Table 1 revises three-iteration runtime from 0.789 to 0.689 seconds. Detailed SSIM/LPIPS trajectories from v2 Table 8 and the Gaussian-reconstruction examples are removed; Figure 4 retains the PSNR/time comparison.

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical candidate-window specifications and computational-complexity reasoning for local kNN: O(N²) global search versus O(NC), described as O(N) with a bounded candidate set. The existing reconstruction, recurrence, and training equations remain equivalent apart from notation and disclosed dimensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: gradient-free recurrent Gaussian refinement, compact initialization, improved rendering efficiency, and generalization across datasets, view counts, and resolutions. The added comparisons chiefly support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning parameter efficiency and initialization quality, and reframes coordinate alignment around spatial centrality rather than temporal video order. The conclusion replaces the kNN scalability limitation with fixed Gaussian count and possible pruning/densification, while retaining saturation after four iterations.

D1.justification: v3 reports publicly released code and pretrained models instead of a future release promise. It adds feature dimensions, Gaussian parameter dimensionality, the CUDA kNN source, and local-search radii. It revises the Small model count from 76M to 77M and removes the explicit Flash Attention 3 and four-GH200 ablation-hardware disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including AnySplat, WorldMirror, YonoSplat, Pointcept, DINOv2, and PyTorch, while removing FlashAttention-3, Point Transformer V2, and XCube references. The overall positioning relative to feed-forward reconstruction and learned optimization remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title from Gaussian Splats to Gaussian Splatting, polishes and shortens prose, adds implementation subheadings, and moves compression discussion into the appendix. Keywords and acknowledgments are added, while the LLM-use disclosure is removed. The overall section sequence and explanatory narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: A different document template changes typography, headers, text width, and placement of figures and tables throughout. v3 adds Table 2, Figure 6, and Table S7, adds a zoomed inset to Figure 4, relocates the compression table, and removes v2 Table 8 and Figures 12–13. Most remaining visual content is reused.

improvement.justification: The added scale and initialization analyses strengthen empirical support, while Table S7 documents a practical speed improvement with a small quality tradeoff. Reported code/model availability and additional implementation details also help reproducibility. These benefits outweigh the loss of detailed refinement metrics and Gaussian visualizations, but the largely unchanged core evidence and limited protocol detail for the new comparisons keep the overall improvement modest.
